what: A parallelogram linkage carries a tray while keeping its orientation nearly constant. Equal side links keep the tray level while its path curves. Physical stops limit the lifting sweep.
try: Reset and run the lift cycle.
Watch the tray edge as it rises and moves sideways.
Compare the motion of a point on the tray with the links rotating below it.
why: Equal opposite sides preserve the tray’s orientation. Its position still follows an arc: keeping an object level does not make its path vertical.
matters: Parallel linkages guide trays, lamps and handling mechanisms.
question: Must a level tray move straight up?
answer: No. Orientation and path are different constraints. Here the tray stays level while its support links sweep arcs.
